The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Radio Presence (1992)
podcast.body: The Killjoys were formed in Hamilton in 1992 by Mike Treblecock. They became a pervasive presence on rock radio and Much Music throughout the mid-1990s. "Hamilton's Killjoy's were pretty much inescapable on rock radio and on much music during the middle of the decade. They were formed in 1992 by Mike Treblecock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Award for Best New Group (1997)
podcast.body: The band was recognized with a Juno Award for Best New Group in 1997, marking a significant achievement in their career. "They also picked up a June for Best New Group in 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup and Continued Reunions (1999-Present)
podcast.body: The Killjoys initially broke up in 1999. However, they have reformed multiple times over the subsequent two decades, a pattern that continues to the present day. "The Killjoy's broke up in 1999, but reformed several times over the next two decades, something that continues even today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guitar Instructor
xref.body: Mike Treblecock, founder of the Killjoys, currently teaches guitar. "Mike Treblecock has now teaching guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
